resources.string: Connecting to Tor and opening your index
Shown while OMNId keeps its index and routers available
Search is available; crawling follows your charger and Wi-Fi settings.
Crawl on battery and mobile data

OMNId reaches Hyphanet through a node\'s FProxy. Leave this empty for a node on this phone, or enter one on your own computer, over Tailscale for instance. A node on this phone stays the fallback. OMNId does not encrypt the way to a node: use one only over a network you trust, such as Tailscale.
That is not a node\'s address: use http://host:port

OMNId reaches I2P through a router: leave this empty for the i2pd app on this phone, or enter a router on your own computer, over Tailscale for instance. The i2pd app stays the fallback. Where the router has SAM on (port 7656), each site you open gets an I2P identity of its own, on 3-hop tunnels OMNId asks for; otherwise every site shares the router\'s HTTP proxy and its one I2P address. The i2pd app ships with SAM off and 1-hop tunnels for its proxy: turn SAM on in its i2pd.conf ([sam] enabled = true), or use a router like the one on your computer. OMNId does not encrypt the way to a router: use one only over a network you trust, such as Tailscale; a router at a Tailscale address is asked only while Tailscale is on.
That is not a router\'s address: use http://host:port

Turn off and pages load far faster over Tor: images are most of what they weigh.

Results in these languages come first. Two-letter codes, best first. Leave this empty for your phone\'s languages.
Use two-letter language codes, such as de, en: five at most.
A page that contains one of these is not indexed, and its links are not followed. One word or phrase per line.
Never crawled, and links to them are not followed. One per line: a host name (its subdomains too), an onion or .i2p address, or a Hyphanet key.
Half the connections: cooler, and lighter on data.
Up to 8 onion sites and 6 web sites at a time.
Twice the connections. Each site still gets one request at a time.
While off, OMNId crawls only while the phone charges on Wi-Fi. Search works either way.

Skips onion sites Ahmia lists for child sexual abuse material. It also lists ordinary ones (Tor\'s blog, Debian, the Guardian); your seeds are crawled whatever it says. Turned off, what it blocked is crawled again; your blocked words and sites still apply.

While on, web pages the crawler fetches come through Tor, like everything the browser opens. Off is faster, but a page found on an onion site could then make your phone fetch an address its author watches, from your own IP.

Finds torrents\' names and file lists on the BitTorrent network. It cannot go through Tor: that network sees your phone\'s address and every torrent it looks up, those found on onion sites too. While off, torrents are listed from their links alone.
Other apps on this phone reach Tor, I2P and Hyphanet through OMNId, as a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy. Nothing goes direct, and each username gets Tor circuits of its own.
Not running: another app holds port %1$d. Apps set to use the proxy would be talking to that app, not OMNId: turn their proxy setting off until this says it runs.
While off, any app on this phone can use the proxy, not only the ones you set up.

Use it with any username, as SOCKS5 credentials or HTTP Basic:

%1$s

Apps with different usernames get different Tor circuits.

A torrent app connects to the BitTorrent network directly, outside Tor: that network sees your address and which torrent you asked for. OMNId hands over only the torrent\'s hash and name, without the trackers and peers a page can put in a link.
